prompt: On this platform, who decides whether case matters in a cloze answer?

choices.text: The grader, by a default that applies to every question
choices.why: A default would answer a teaching question for everybody.

choices.text: The question
choices.why: Right. It declares ignore_case, and the grader does what it says.

choices.text: The student, by typing carefully
choices.why: The rule is set before anybody answers.

choices.text: The language of the page
choices.why: Case rules belong to the question, not the locale.

prompt: Why does this platform feed every question its own answer key before publishing it?

choices.text: To measure how long marking takes
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: To translate the key into Portuguese
choices.why: Keys are not translated.

choices.text: To decide the question's difficulty from how fast it is marked
choices.why: Difficulty comes from students' answers, later.

choices.text: Because a wrong key is the failure nothing else would catch
choices.why: Right. A schema check passes a question nobody can answer correctly.

prompt: Under release 2026.10.1, how many of the 30 evaluation questions got a right reply?
Why does evalrun.py keep the sources each reply was given, as well as the reply?

choices.text: Because the grader needs them to compute cost
choices.why: Cost comes from tokens, not from sources.

choices.text: To check that the database has not changed
choices.why: That is not what the run is for.

choices.text: To regrade it later without the model
choices.why: Right: another method, the same replies, no second call. Lessons 9 to 12 grade this same file.

choices.text: Because the model needs them on the next run
choices.why: Every run retrieves afresh.

prompt: The reply "You have thirty days after delivery to return it" failed both comparisons. Why?

choices.text: It is a paraphrase
choices.why: Right. No normalisation reaches different words for the same meaning.

choices.text: It has no citation
choices.why: It cites [1]; and the comparison does not look at citations.

choices.text: The normalisation lowercased the fact but not the reply, so the two never met
choices.why: It squashes both sides the same way.

choices.text: It is too long
choices.why: Length plays no part in the comparison.

prompt: For which expected answer is a deterministic comparison the right tool?

choices.text: Why a return was refused, in the support team's words
choices.why: Free text has many right wordings.

choices.text: A summary of a conversation
choices.why: A summary has endless right versions.

choices.text: An error code such as E-4102
choices.why: Right. It has one form, and any other is wrong.

choices.text: A polite greeting to the customer
choices.why: Politeness has no single wording.

choices.text: It costs more tokens

choices.text: It breaks the trace

prompt: What kind of faithfulness can the numbers rule check with certainty?

choices.text: That every claim in the reply is true
choices.why: Only the numbers, and only that they appear somewhere in the sources.

choices.text: That every number is the right one for the question asked
choices.why: A number from the wrong row of the right table passes.

choices.text: That the reply cites the right source
choices.why: It looks at all the sources together.

choices.text: That no figure in the reply came from outside the sources
choices.why: Right. A price that is in no source came from nowhere.

prompt: What does a rule need that a comparison with a fact does not?

choices.text: A model to run it
choices.why: It is a Python function.

choices.text: Nothing written in advance for each question
choices.why: Right. A rule is a property of every good reply, so it can judge replies nobody wrote a key for.

choices.text: A person to approve it
choices.why: It decides on its own.

choices.text: An answer key for each question
choices.why: That is what the fact comparison needs, not the rule.

prompt: Why can the rules run on every reply in production, and not on a sample?

choices.text: They cost microseconds and no tokens
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Production has few replies
choices.why: The reason is the price per check, whatever the volume.

choices.text: They run inside the provider
choices.why: They run in the application or a job.

choices.text: Samples are not allowed by the LGPD
choices.why: Nothing in the law says that.

prompt: Not one check failed in 1,221 replies. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: The checks are useless and can be removed
choices.why: A tripwire's value is not in how often it goes off.

choices.text: The assistant is perfect
choices.why: Fourteen of thirty eval replies were wrong.

choices.text: The checks were not run
choices.why: check_week.py printed every count.

choices.text: Keep them as tripwires
choices.why: Right: the zeros are the stand-in. A new model or prompt can start breaking them overnight.

prompt: One reply in ten thousand fails a citation check. One in fifty starts failing on a release day. Which is the alert?

choices.why: That is noise.

choices.text: Both equally

choices.text: The rate that changed with the release
choices.why: Right. Watch the rate, not single failures.

choices.text: Neither: citation checks cannot alert
choices.why: Their rate can, in lesson 16.

prompt: How many replies of the week did check_week.py read, both releases together?
A team loosens its fact comparison to accept any reply sharing two words with the fact. What has it bought?

choices.text: A comparison that understands meaning
choices.why: Shared words are not shared meaning.

choices.text: Fewer false failures and no new false passes
choices.why: Any reply mentioning 'days' and 'delivery' would pass.

choices.text: Nothing: two words is the same as exact
choices.why: It is far looser.

choices.text: Paraphrases pass, and so do many wrong replies
choices.why: Right. A loosening that changes meaning is a different, weaker test.
